step1_analysis.description: An inverter-based amplifier core with an active push-pull pseudo-resistor feedback network (XM1, XM2). It provides extremely high DC resistance for low-frequency high-pass filtering in biomedical applications, while allowing fast recovery from large artifacts by drastically lowering its resistance during large signal swings.

paper_reference.title: An Adaptive ENG Amplifier for Tripolar Cuff Electrodes

DC_Power.description: Quiescent power dissipation of the amplifier core.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Based on sky130 NMOS/PMOS parameters at VDD/2. In a fully optimized ultra-low-power design, L would be much larger to reduce this current.

V_trip.description: Self-biased DC operating point at the input (virtual ground).

sky130_expected.calculation: A symmetric inverter with VDD=1.8V trips near VDD/2.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined by the relative drive strengths of XM3 and XM4.

Inverter_Gain.description: Open-loop DC voltage gain of the inverter stage.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Intrinsic gain of a short-channel (L=0.5u) inverter in sky130.

R_eq_DC.description: Effective small-signal feedback resistance at DC.

sky130_expected.calculation: R_eq = 1 / (gm1 + gm2) in deep subthreshold. gm ≈ 1.8nA/V -> R_eq ≈ 550 MΩ.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends exponentially on Vth and subthreshold slope. Provides the huge resistance needed for sub-Hz high-pass poles.

V_VE_swing.description: Output voltage swing required to sink/source 1uA of input current, demonstrating non-linear recovery.

sky130_expected.calculation: To sink 1uA, PMOS needs Vsg ≈ 0.48V. V_VE = V_trip - Vsg ≈ 0.9 - 0.48 = 0.42V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Shows the active pseudo-resistor turning on to handle large currents, drastically lowering its resistance.

step3_testbench.description: Measures DC operating point, AC open-loop gain, effective feedback resistance, and large-signal DC transfer characteristics.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Active Pseudo-Resistor Amplifier Core Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

* Parameters from netlist
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u

* DUT
XM3 VE II VSS GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 VE II VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM2 VDD VE II GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM1 VSS VE II VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}

* Sources
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VVSS VSS 0 0
VGND GND 0 0

* Input Current Source for AC and DC sweep
* AC 1A allows direct reading of transimpedance (Ohms) as voltage magnitude
Iin II 0 DC 0 AC 1

.control
  * 1. Operating Point
  op
  let v_trip = v(II)
  let pwr = -i(VVDD) * 1.8
  print v_trip pwr
  
  * 2. AC Analysis
  ac dec 10 1m 1G
  * Inverter Gain = v(VE) / v(II)
  let inv_gain = mag(v(VE)) / mag(v(II))
  let inv_gain_db = 20 * log10(inv_gain)
  * Effective Resistance = v(VE) / Iin = v(VE) (since Iin=1)
  let r_eq = mag(v(VE))
  
  meas ac dc_inv_gain_db find inv_gain_db at=1m
  meas ac dc_r_eq find r_eq at=1m
  meas ac r_eq_1k find r_eq at=1k
  
  * 3. DC Sweep (Large Signal Non-linear Resistance)
  dc Iin -1u 1u 10n
  meas dc v_ve_plus find v(VE) at=1u
  meas dc v_ve_minus find v(VE) at=-1u
  
  quit
.endc
.end
